pr_title: Display custom data layer names in the tile set editor properties
pr_body: While the custom data layer properties in the tile set editor were listed like this: They are now listed like this, exposing their assigned names: This provides a great deal of comfort as opposed to having to perform a manual lookup for the custom data layers in order to determine which is which. * *Bugsquad edit, fixes: #76733*
pr_comments:
Hi, thanks for trying to solve this but this is not the right solution.
Changing the property name will break compatibility, and will cause loss of data when renaming a property. It cannot be done that way.

Instead, we should implement an inspector plugin that displays names instead of numbers, but that's quite a bit tricky to implement.

> Hi, thanks for trying to solve this but this is not the right solution. Changing the property name will break compatibility, and will cause loss of data when renaming a property. It cannot be done that way.
> 
> Instead, we should implement an inspector plugin that displays names instead of numbers, but that's quite a bit tricky to implement.

Ah, now I understand why it wasn't there in the first place, it seemed like a too easy thing to 'forget'.

> Ah, now I understand why it wasn't there in the first place, it seemed like a too easy thing to 'forget'.

Yeah, trust me, I've been wanting since day one to have the custom name displayed there. It's simply a bit complex to implement.

I believe we have two ways to solve this:
1) implement an inspector plugin to do it. This is a local solution to the problem, but might need bit of code duplication (basically, recreating part of the inspector)
2) add a way to display a custom name for a property in the inspector. This is a global solution, that could probably be used elsewhere. But it touches more things in the codebase, which could lead to issues.

Thanks for explaining this. Since I'm totally new to the code base, it's a bit too much of a stretch for me at this moment to further help with this.

I have to say though that the second solution sounds like the wiser one. It just makes a lot of sense as a generic feature.

issue_context.title: Custom data layers don't have the correct name displayed in the TileSet window
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.2.stable.official [7a0977ce2]

### System information

Windows 11

### Issue description

Currently in Godot 4 you can create powerful Custom Data Layers. But when applying changes to that data in the tileset window (for example selecting true/false value for specific tiles) the name for specific custom data layer is the index number instead of actual name set in Custom Data Layers.

![obraz](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40697587/236290993-94033f76-bd0d-4c77-9cc6-f327b11c99ba.png)
![obraz](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40697587/236291159-5ad50c7c-eea9-4c68-8c78-13949f96a0ac.png)


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create tilemap node
2. Create/assign tileset to that tilemap node
3. Create new Custom Data Layer for that TileSet
4. Go to TileSet window, press select and select any tile in the tileset
5. See that custom data layer works, but has incorrect name

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments: I can take a look at this.

I've looked into the problem and it seems to rely on the inspector properties of the custom data layers. Unfortunately, I'm not sure how we can overwrite the labels as it seems we can't change the property labels themselves. I may have to leave this to someone whos more experienced in Godot's codebase. :(
@cjapar2  Are you still working on this?
Got it, I shall take a look now
Pushing is issue, as it would be really useful to see the names.
Also encountering this, it makes the Custom Data functionality far less useful if it isn't clear what the properties actually are

review_comments: The condition is unnecessary. If name is empty, it will display `""` the same.

Well, the idea behind this is to keep the existing behavior unchanged for nameless fields. That's exactly what's happening in the fourth field in the second screenshot. 

In other words: the empty check determines whether to insert a colon separator between de field index and name.

Otherwise, the index would be followed by a colon with nothing on the right hand.
Ah right, I didn't notice the color. Sorry.
